gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the hair-dryer outlet on Ceptics' $49.99 LX-C2000 combo does not work with dryers that have circuit boards, such as Dyson and Shark FlexStyle (Ceptics points those to its $129.99 pure-sine VC-S2000), or that the low-watt '200W' outlet on combos like Ceptics LX2-M2000 and TESSAN's 2000W unit does not convert voltage at all.
standout_why: I checked Global Plugs (voltage-converter-vs-adapter), the VoltWander FAQ and Gadget Flow's TESSAN TC03 review. Global Plugs names no combo products, never says combos have separate converting and non-converting outlets, and calls combos 25-100 W only. VoltWander names no combo products and has no hair-dryer exclusions by type. Gadget Flow says only that the TC03 'won't run a hair dryer'. ChatGPT's answer said compact converters can't handle hair dryers, which misses the 2000 W combos and their Dyson exclusion. I could not read the TESSAN, FOVAL and EPICKA manuals.plus PDFs (image-only or 403), the Digital Camera World Ceptics review (body didn't load), travelpowerpro (certificate error) or AAA (no body), so a 3 is not safe.
decides: The pick depends on the device the shopper plans to plug in. Phones, cameras and other small 110 V-only electronics up to 250 W: TESSAN TC03 ($43.99). A US hair dryer with a mechanical switch: a combo with a 2000 W outlet, such as Ceptics LX-C2000 ($49.99) or TESSAN's 2000W combo ($45.99). A Dyson or Shark FlexStyle: Ceptics's own copy rules out the LX-C2000, and the only one I found from these two makers that it names for Dyson use is the pure-sine Ceptics VC-S2000 ($129.99), with nothing else plugged in. Laptops and phone chargers marked 100-240 V belong in the non-converting outlet or USB ports. The 200 W units ChatGPT showed ($59.99 Ceptics, $41.97 TESSAN) are wrong for any hair dryer.
